title: LEEDS CITY COUNCIL: Consultation opens on 20mph limits outside city schools
summary: Parents, residents and drivers are being asked for their views on lower speed limits on roads outside 14 primary schools in Leeds. The consultation runs for six weeks.
body_html:
Leeds City Council has opened a six-week consultation on proposals to bring in 20mph limits on roads outside 14 primary schools.

A report to the council's executive board says the schools were chosen after a review of collision records and of requests from head teachers and parent groups over the past three years.

The proposals include new signs and road markings and, outside four of the schools, raised crossings. The council puts the cost at £310,000, to be met from its road safety budget.

A council spokesperson said: "We want to hear from everyone who uses these roads, including people who drive through the areas at school times."

Responses can be made online or in writing. The executive board is expected to consider the results in the spring.

title: BRADFORD COUNCIL: Library opening hours to change from April
summary: Seven libraries in the Bradford district will open later on weekday mornings and stay open longer on Saturdays from April, under changes agreed by councillors.
body_html:
Seven libraries in the Bradford district will change their opening hours from April, after councillors approved a new timetable.

Under the changes, the libraries will open at 10am instead of 9am from Monday to Friday and will stay open until 4pm on Saturdays, two hours later than now.

A report to the council's executive said visitor counts showed few people using the libraries before 10am, while Saturday afternoons were among the busiest times.

The council said no library would close and no posts would be lost. Opposition councillors asked for the new hours to be reviewed after a year, which the executive agreed.

title: KIRKLEES COUNCIL: Planning committee approves 120 homes on former mill site
summary: Plans for 120 homes on the site of a disused textile mill have been approved by Kirklees Council's strategic planning committee, despite objections about traffic.
body_html:
Kirklees Council's strategic planning committee has approved plans for 120 homes on the site of a former textile mill.

The scheme includes 24 affordable homes, a children's play area and a new footpath along the river. The original mill building, which is not listed, will be demolished.

The council received 68 objections, most of them about traffic on the narrow road that leads to the site. Highways officers told the committee the developer would pay for a new junction and a pedestrian crossing.

The committee voted seven to two in favour. Work could start next year if conditions on drainage and contamination are met.

title: SHEFFIELD CITY COUNCIL: Scrutiny panel to review changes to bin collections
summary: A Sheffield City Council scrutiny panel will look at how the move to three-weekly general waste collections has worked, after more than 2,000 complaints in its first two months.
body_html:
A Sheffield City Council scrutiny panel is to review the move to three-weekly general waste collections.

The change began in the autumn. A report to the panel says the council received 2,140 complaints in the first two months, most about missed collections on routes that had been redrawn.

Recycling rates rose by four percentage points over the same period, the report says.

The panel will hear from waste managers and from residents' groups before making recommendations to the cabinet member for the environment.

title: LEEDS CITY COUNCIL: Councillors to debate future of three community centres
summary: The future of three community centres in Leeds will be debated at a full council meeting next week, after a review found they need repairs costing more than £1m.
body_html:
Leeds City Council will debate the future of three community centres at its full council meeting next week.

A review of the council's buildings found the three centres need repairs costing £1.2m between them. Options in the report include handing the buildings to community groups, selling them, or repairing them over five years.

title: BRADFORD COUNCIL: Budget gap of £18m forecast for next year
summary: Bradford Council expects an £18m gap between spending and income next year, according to a report to its executive, which sets out savings and a possible council tax rise.
body_html:
Bradford Council is forecasting a budget gap of £18m for the next financial year.

A report to the executive says rising demand for adult and children's social care accounts for most of the gap. Energy costs and pay awards make up the rest.

The report proposes £11m of savings, including fewer agency staff and a review of the council's office buildings, and says a council tax rise is likely to be needed to close the remaining gap.

The executive will set out its draft budget next month, followed by a public consultation.

title: KIRKLEES COUNCIL: Town centre parking charges to be reviewed
summary: Kirklees Council is to review parking charges in its town centres, after traders said higher charges introduced last year were keeping shoppers away.
body_html:
Kirklees Council is to review parking charges in its town centre car parks.

Charges rose by an average of 40p an hour last year. A petition signed by more than 1,500 people and backed by several traders' groups asked for the rise to be reversed.

The council's cabinet member for highways said the review would look at usage figures from every car park before any decision was made.

The review is due to report in the summer.

title: SHEFFIELD CITY COUNCIL: Tree planting plan sets a target for every ward
summary: Sheffield City Council has published a tree planting plan with a target for every ward in the city, as part of its response to the climate emergency it declared.
body_html:
Sheffield City Council has set out a plan to plant trees in every ward in the city over the next ten years.

The plan includes street trees, new woodland on council land and free trees for schools and community groups.

Each ward has its own target, based on the amount of tree cover it has now. Wards with the least cover would get the most new trees.

title: LEEDS CITY COUNCIL: Executive board backs plan for new homelessness support hub
summary: Leeds City Council's executive board has backed plans for a support hub for people who are homeless or at risk of losing their home, bringing several services under one roof.
body_html:
Leeds City Council's executive board has backed plans for a new homelessness support hub in the city centre.

The hub would bring together housing advice, health services and support from voluntary groups in one building, open seven days a week.

A report to the board says the number of households in temporary accommodation in the city has risen by a quarter in two years.

The council will now look for a suitable building and expects to open the hub within 18 months.

title: SHEFFIELD CITY COUNCIL: Former council office block to be sold
summary: Sheffield City Council plans to sell a former office block in the city centre that has been empty since staff moved to a new building, with the money going towards repairs elsewhere.
body_html:
Sheffield City Council plans to sell a former office block in the city centre.

The building has been empty for two years, since staff moved to the council's main offices. A report to the cabinet says keeping it empty costs about £250,000 a year in security, insurance and business rates.

The money from the sale would go towards repairs to other council buildings, the report says.

Opposition councillors have asked whether the building could be used for housing instead.

title: NEWCASTLE CITY COUNCIL: Cabinet agrees ten-year plan for riverside events
summary: Newcastle City Council's cabinet has agreed a ten-year plan for events on the riverside, which aims to bring more visitors to the city outside the summer months.
body_html:
Newcastle City Council's cabinet has agreed a ten-year plan for events on the city's riverside.

The plan aims to spread events across the year, with a winter festival, a food market and more use of the riverside for sport.

A report to the cabinet says businesses on the riverside see far fewer visitors between October and March than in summer.

The council will seek funding from partners and sponsors and says no new money from the council budget is planned.

title: SUNDERLAND CITY COUNCIL: Plans lodged for 85 riverside flats
summary: A planning application for 85 flats on a vacant riverside plot in Sunderland has been lodged with the city council. Residents have four weeks to comment.
body_html:
A developer has applied to Sunderland City Council for permission to build 85 flats on a vacant plot beside the river.

The application includes a six-storey building, a public walkway along the river and space for a small shop or café on the ground floor.

Residents and businesses have four weeks to comment. The application is expected to go before the planning committee in the spring.

title: GATESHEAD COUNCIL: Leisure centre to close for six months of repairs
summary: A leisure centre in Gateshead will close for six months from the spring while its roof and pool are repaired. The council says swimming lessons will move to other centres.
body_html:
Gateshead Council says one of its leisure centres will close for six months from the spring for repairs.

The work includes a new roof and repairs to the pool's filtration system. The council says the repairs cannot be done while the centre is open.

Swimming lessons and club bookings will move to two other council centres during the closure.

title: NORTHUMBERLAND COUNTY COUNCIL: Rural bus routes to be retendered
summary: Northumberland County Council will retender 12 subsidised rural bus routes when the current contracts end in the summer, and says no route will be withdrawn.
body_html:
Northumberland County Council is to retender 12 subsidised rural bus routes.

The current contracts end in the summer. A report to the council's cabinet says the routes carry about 4,000 passengers a week, many of them older people travelling to appointments and shops.

The council says no route will be withdrawn as part of the process, but timetables may change.

Bus operators have until the end of next month to submit bids.

title: BIRMINGHAM CITY COUNCIL: Consultation on changes to household recycling centres
summary: Birmingham City Council has launched a consultation on changes to its household recycling centres, including a booking system at the busiest sites.
body_html:
Birmingham City Council has launched a consultation on changes to its household recycling centres.

The proposals include a booking system at the two busiest sites and longer opening hours on summer evenings.

The council says queues at the busiest sites have backed up onto main roads at weekends.

The consultation runs for eight weeks. A council spokesperson said residents without internet access would be able to book by phone.

title: COVENTRY CITY COUNCIL: Auditor's report on accounts to go before audit committee
summary: The external auditor's annual report on Coventry City Council's accounts will be presented to the council's audit committee. The report is embargoed until the council publishes it.
body_html:
The external auditor's annual report on Coventry City Council's accounts is to be presented to the council's audit and procurement committee.

The report covers the council's financial statements and its arrangements for getting value for money.

The council has asked for coverage to be held until it publishes the report on its website.

title: NOTTINGHAM CITY COUNCIL: Tram extension study goes to transport committee
summary: A study into extending one of Nottingham's tram lines to a new housing area will be considered by the city council's transport committee next week.
body_html:
A study into extending one of Nottingham's tram lines will go before the city council's transport committee next week.

The study looks at three possible routes to a new housing development on the edge of the city, and estimates costs for each.

Councillors will be asked whether to spend £400,000 on a more detailed business case.

The study says any extension would depend on government funding.

title: CARDIFF COUNCIL: Changes to school admissions approved for September
summary: Cardiff Council's cabinet has approved changes to admissions for three primary schools from September, after a consultation with parents.
body_html:
Cardiff Council's cabinet has approved changes to admissions for three primary schools from September.

Two of the schools will take more pupils each year, and catchment areas around the third will be redrawn.

The council said the changes follow a consultation in which most parents who responded supported the plans.

Parents of children starting school in September will be told which school their child has a place at in April.

title: GWYNEDD COUNCIL: Welsh language services plan goes out to consultation
summary: Gwynedd Council has opened a consultation on its plan for providing services in Welsh. The story includes a Welsh language version.
body_html:
Gwynedd Council has opened a consultation on its new plan for providing council services in Welsh.

The plan sets out how the council will offer services in Welsh to residents online, by phone and face to face.

The consultation will be open for eight weeks. Residents can respond online or at local libraries.

A council spokesperson said: "We want to hear from everyone who uses our services."

The scheme includes a wider promenade, new seating and planting, and changes to traffic on the seafront road.

The council says it will hold drop-in sessions for residents and businesses once the detailed designs are ready.
